_meta: A small reference population of people, each described by a set of tags (profession and traits). We estimate the probability of a hypothesis by the fraction of the population it matches. The point is the conjunction rule: the probability of 'A and B' can never exceed the probability of A alone, because the people who are both A and B are a subset of the people who are A. Yet a more detailed, representative-sounding hypothesis ('a bank teller who is also an activist') feels more probable than the broad one ('a bank teller') -- the conjunction fallacy. pairs lists (broad_tag, extra_tag) hypotheses to compare: the single tag vs the conjunction of both. Every probability here is an exact count over the population.
